data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A redundant monolith is superior in resilience when the primary failure mode is 'resource exhaustion' or 'coordinated load spikes', as it can dynamically reallocate internal capacity that decentralized services cannot share.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The failure is caused by a logic bug rather than a resource spike.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith's load balancer is itself a single point of failure.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a decentralized network, a spike in traffic to one service can kill it while neighboring services have idle capacity.
